title: ops-reliability-swift-onboard-experiment-canvas
content:
Purpose:
Rapidly onboard partner feature teams into a lightweight SLO and reliability workflow using a repeatable lab experiment format. This doc sketches the 6-week pilot ("Swift Onboard") that tests whether short, hands-on lab sessions + a tiny runbook reduce onboarding time and improve signal quality for early SLO adoption.

Background / motivation:
- We repeatedly see long handoffs when feature teams attempt to add model-serving SLOs: unclear owners, missing metrics, dashboards that don’t map to product stakes.
- Hypothesis: a structured 3-session lab with pre-work, live pairing, and a followup retro + template artifacts will cut time-to-first-SLO by >=50% and produce usable dashboards + one actionable runbook per service.

Scope (pilot):
- Target 3 feature teams (embedding-ops, chat-router, analytics-ingest) over 6 weeks.
- Only covering availability and p50/p95 latency SLOs for model serving endpoints and core inference queueing.
- Excludes platform-wide policy work (that follows pilot results).

Success outcomes / KPIs (experiment-level):
- Time from kickoff to first SLO + dashboard <= 10 business days for 2/3 teams.
- SLO definitions accepted by teams and SREs without >2 rounds of revision.
- One runbook and one lightweight alerting policy per service created and verified in staging by EoP (end of pilot).

Core components / deliverables:
- Lab agenda (3 sessions):
  - Pre-lab checklist (1 day): metrics access, example traffic, Confluence template filled ~30% by team.
  - Session A (2h): framing, service stake mapping, draft SLOs, assign owners.
  - Session B (2h, 3–5 days later): instrumentation pairing, metrics queries, dashboard skeleton built.
  - Session C (1.5h): review SLI/SLO, alert thresholds, runbook draft, canary plan for rollout.
- Templates: SLO definition template, dashboard skeleton (Grafana JSON snippet), runbook checklist, incident play snippet for model degradation.
- Measurement harness: small artifact repo with example queries and a test harness to inject synthetic load for verification.

Roles & responsibilities:
- SRE Lab Coach (Aisha Morales): design lab, facilitate sessions, own synthesis artifacts.
- Metrics Engineer (Jae Park): help build dashboard skeletons and validate SLIs.
- Observability SME (Martin Li): confirm tracing/latency buckets are set and recommend aggregation windows.
- Team leads (one per feature team): bring product stakes, accept SLOs, own rollout.
- Release/Platform contact (Riley Thompson): help wire canary and deployment gating.

6-week pilot timeline (high level):
- Week 0: kickoff + pre-lab checklist assigned.
- Week 1: Session A for team 1; pre-work check.
- Week 2: Session B for team 1; Session A for team 2.
- Week 3: Session C for team 1; Session B for team 2; Session A for team 3.
- Week 4: Session C for team 2; Session B for team 3; mid-pilot retro (SRE + product).
- Week 5: Session C for team 3; finalize runbooks; staging verification; prepare pilot report.

Runbooks & artifacts to produce per team (minimal viable):
- "SLO one-pager": stakeholder, SLA mapping (if any), SLI definition, SLO value, measurement window, owner, rollback policy.
- Dashboard: p50/p95 latency, request rate, error rate, infra KPIs (GPU queue length, memory).
- Alert policy: threshold + signal, burn rate protection notes, on-call routing.
- Small test harness repo with readme and a load script.

Communication & cadence:
- Weekly 30m sync between SRE lab coaches + metrics engineer (Wednesdays).
- Dedicated Slack channel per team (#sre-lab-<team>) with short daily async check-ins during active week.
- Mid-pilot demo session (30m) to stakeholders and product managers.

Risk register (top-level):
- Risk: Observability gaps (missing metrics). Mitigation: Pre-lab checklist with gating; if missing, build a light exporter during Session B.
- Risk: Team bandwidth. Mitigation: Pre-schedule sessions; provide SRE pairing time and accept partial artifacts (we iterate).
- Risk: Confusion about SLO scope. Mitigation: mapping exercise during Session A explicitly ties SLOs to customer impact and investment tradeoffs.

Evaluation & next steps (post-pilot):
- Compile pilot report: time-to-first-SLO, artifacts produced, lessons learned, recommended central templates.
- Decide go/no-go to scale: if KPIs met, prepare a "SLO-onboarding-kit" and a 12-week rollout plan for broader org.
- Small follow-up experiments: automated pre-check tool for metric availability, a one-click dashboard instantiation flow.

Quick checklists (copyable):
- Pre-lab checklist:
  - [ ] SRE and team lead scheduled for Session A (2h)
  - [ ] Metrics read access granted to SRE coach
  - [ ] Example traffic saved (1 hour sample)
  - [ ] Existing alerts listed in Confluence

- Session B pairing checklist:
  - [ ] Confirm metric queries return expected values
  - [ ] Dashboard panel for p95 latency created
  - [ ] Synthetic load recipe validated in staging

Notes / open questions to track:
- Which teams should be prioritized after pilot (criteria: customer impact, velocity, ops debt).
- Longer-term: how do we version SLOs with model rollouts and quantization changes? (input for Product + Research).
- Should Dedicated / Private customers follow a slightly different lab (networking and privacy checks)?

Appendix (quick links):
- Confluence SLO template (linked above), sample Grafana JSON, onboarding repo stub: github.com/redwood-inference/slo-onboard-stub

Owner / contact: Aisha Morales (sre-labs@redwood.ai).
